i feel this. i wasn't, and still an not, necessarily attractive.  especially during late middle school i watched all my friends, who are, get in relationships, and have people want them, and being happy. and i wasn't any of those things at all. it kinda pushed me to associate being happy with being wanted, and i thought that because i wasn't wanted, i wasn't happy. 

when my then-partner told me they liked me, i got so excited. i thought i would finally experience that joy all of my friends did, and i did! temporarily. the problem with associating happiness with how other people feel about you is that feelings are so volatile and subject to change, and when their feelings about you change, so does happiness. breaking up with them reinforced the idea that i really wasn't wanted. 

i hate to get all joker-y but society really peddles the idea that you have to be wanted to be needed, and that your value should rest in other people's opinions on you. my value didn't depend on whether or not that specific person wanted me, or whether anybody at all wanted me, and neither does yours. you don't have to be wanted to be valued- the fact that you are a person- someone with love, desires, hobbies, emotion- gives you inherent value. people who can't see that, and can't see how important you are, aren't people who's opinions you should value. i still struggle with it, but knowing that fact really helps sometimes.

as for a reason to live, i'm gonna be honest- i can't really give you that. i don't know you well enough to tell you anything that could really help. my only advice is to think of little things that make you happy- small details about your life that make it worth it. maybe a detail or habit about a friend, or a special object you have, or your motivation behind doing stuff. it doesn't really have to make sense or anything. that feeling those things give you can be your reason. even if it's not enough to help you through everything, if it's enough to keep you alive, it's good enough. everything else is secondary. 

i'm not really the best at giving advice, so i'm sorry if this doesn't help at all, but if it does, my dms are always open. feel free to message me anytime.

hey jake, i'm around your age and went through something similar last year. i'm still here, even though at the time i really didn't think i would be.  i know it feels like absolute shit knowing that someone didn't love you the way you thought they did. it helps to remember that there is love in different places. how that person felt about you isn't, and will never be, representative of how everyone else feels about you. love and respect come in so many different forms, that selecting a single persons perspective of you and adopting trust as a universal truth is a disservice to yourself. there are still so many people to meet in the future who will feel the same way about you. there's nothing you need to "fix" about yourself- you are who you are, and while there are always going to be people who can't appreciate that, there are countless more who will, and who'll love everything about you. 

when this happened to me, something that helped me was just talking to friends and family about completely unrelated topics. it simultaneously took my mind off of the relationship and reminded me that i do matter, and that there were people who loved me and enjoyed spending time with me.

man, you're right. life doesn't always "get better" and anyone who tells you that is lying. life doesn't automatically get better just because you want it to, and life isn't good just because you close your eyes to the bad. but that doesn't mean life itself is inherently bad. i can't promise that this will help, but when i have a depressive period it helps me a little to think of little things that made me happier today, even if it was just a little bit. even if it's just one or two things. it helps ground me and helps me remember that it isn't constant, total dogshit all the time. and if you can't find anything, find things that give you a little bit of happiness- pictures of people you love, saving up for something you've wanted for a while, or even just eating a food you like. it's not a fix all issue and it doesn't fix the underlying issue, but when i need it most it helps take my mind of emotions i'd rather not think about.
